summary: Unexpected role assignment detected after user interacted with third-party marketing iframe
description: Issue summary: Multiple internal employees reported receiving elevated service roles (service/trial-admin) in their accounts within minutes of visiting a recently deployed marketing landing page. Impact: Potential unauthorized privilege grants to internal service identities and several human accounts; risk of configuration changes and sensitive data access. Detection: Report came via Slack #security-alerts from two engineers who noticed new role bindings in the IAM audit logs shortly after clicking a promotional popup embedded as an iframe on the marketing page. This ticket captures triage steps, artifacts, and containment actions.
timeline: 2026-03-10T09:45:22Z: Engineer A reports unexpected admin access to internal tool via Slack
2026-03-10T09:47:10Z: Initial IAM audit logs show role.grant events for org:service-123 and user:eng-alice
2026-03-10T09:55:00Z: Security triage team added to thread, provisional containment started
2026-03-10T10:15:00Z: Ingress logs show POST to /api/invite-proxy originating from marketing-iframe origin header
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Visit marketing landing page https://promo.redwood.team/offer (observed in prod-us-west)
2) A consent-styled iframe loads with origin https://promo-assets.thirdparty.com
3) Click the blue CTA in the iframe (observed by reporting users)
4) Within 1-2 minutes, check IAM audit logs for role.grant events tied to the click-time session
evidence_logs: iam-audit: role.grant by service-account svc-marketing-bridge at 2026-03-10T09:46:08Z for resource service/trial-admin (event_id: a1f5c9)
web-frontend: user session cookie set: sid=eyJld... (truncated) at 2026-03-10T09:45:18Z
k8s-audit: serviceaccount/redwood-marketing-bridge created token at 2026-03-10T09:42:00Z (pod: marketing-bridge-57d7)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Third-party iframe invokes our invite API via a CORS-enabled endpoint using a bridged service account (marketing-bridge) that was mis-scoped.
Hypothesis B: A malicious asset replaced the iframe content post-deploy; marketing-bridge service account key exposed or created in CI during deployment.
Checked: Confirmed marketing-team deploy PR referenced promo-assets CDN URL (marketing-team/deploy#342).
Checked: marketing-bridge service account last key creation 2026-03-10T09:40:50Z from CI runner ip 34.120.7.9 (CI job: marketing/promo-build#876)
Found: invite-proxy controller allowed POST from origin header without CSRF challenge for internal invite endpoint (config: ingress/allow-list missing for promo-assets domain).
Observed: role.grant calls originate from service account svc-marketing-bridge which has iam:roles/editor in its binding—overly permissive.
Session traces: user sessions used single-use tokens issued by invite-proxy, TTL 24h; no device binding observed.
actions_taken: 1) Rotated keys for service account svc-marketing-bridge and revoked active tokens (2026-03-10T10:05Z).
2) Disabled invite-proxy endpoint (ingress rule) for promo-assets.origin (2026-03-10T10:10Z).
3) Reverted marketing deployment to previous stable tag (marketing-team/deploy revert#343) and blocked promo-assets CDN domain in WAF (2026-03-10T10:22Z).
4) Temporarily removed iam:roles/editor binding from svc-marketing-bridge; replaced with narrow role allowing only metrics write (2026-03-10T11:00Z).
5) Forced MFA revalidation for affected human accounts and audited recent privileged actions (2026-03-10T11:30Z).

Miguel Ortega - 2026-03-11T09:00Z: Follow-up: Confirmed no anomalous writes to customer-facing datastore; all affected role.grant events were limited to internal/test services.

resolution: Containment complete: marketing iframe asset removed, marketing-bridge keys rotated, invite-proxy temporarily disabled and restricted. Next steps: run a full IAM audit for the last 72 hours, rotate CI runner tokens, add ingress allowlist and CSRF protections to invite endpoints, and perform a scoped postmortem (owner: Security Team). No evidence of external data exfiltration found as of 2026-03-12.
